The target is therefore emotional state and autonomic arousal rather than social communication, gaze or motor stereotypy, which distinguishes this study from nearly all of the corpus and connects it plausibly to the clinical problem it addresses: the medications at issue are prescribed largely for irritability and agitation, so a continuous measure of affective state and arousal is the right construct for titrating them. Three problems attach to the execution. The mood labels for thermal images of these particular children must have been assigned by someone, and the paper never says who or how - so a five-category emotional ground truth exists with no stated provenance, in a population whose facial expression is itself atypical. Skin temperature is confounded with ambient conditions and exertion across four physically different capture settings with no compensation. And no feature importance is reported for the severity classifiers, so whether the discriminative information lies in mood or in temperature - a question with entirely different clinical implications - is unknown.

**S-131** [local_0f5a351e] — *Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder*

Nominally craniofacial morphology; operationally, whatever separates an autism-labelled image folder from a folder of web-search results. The motivating claims are specific and measurable - broader upper faces, wider eyes, shorter nasal bridges, narrower cheeks - but nothing in the pipeline measures any of them: no landmarks are detected, no distances or ratios computed, and the models receive whole RGB images. What the networks can key on is unconstrained and includes apparent age, sex, ancestry, expression, pose, resolution, compression, lighting and background, all of which are free to differ between two folders built by different routes. The paper's third stated contribution was to analyse which facial features drive detection, which would have been the direct test of its own premise; that analysis does not appear.

**S-132** [local_786b6280] — *Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features*

Structural and quantitative properties of spontaneous speech, operationalised as six standard psycholinguistic descriptors: mean length of utterance, mean length of turn, mean word length, number of utterances, total number of words and number of different words. Two design decisions distinguish this from a generic bag-of-features approach. Each feature was computed both for the child alone and as a ratio to the investigator's value in the same session, and the two versions were compared empirically to see which carried more information - a construct-level question about whether autistic children's speech differs absolutely or relative to their conversational partner's. And the count-based features were used only in ratio form to normalise for transcript length. The results locate the discriminative information in utterance and turn length and in the child's output relative to the adult's, with typically developing children higher on cMLU, rMLU, rMLT, rUtts and rTNW - a coherent picture of shorter utterances, shorter turns and proportionally less talk. Mean word length carried no signal, and the paper draws the right conclusion, that characters are a poor proxy for lexical complexity and that phonemes or morphemes would be the correct unit. The construct that this cannot separate from autism is expressive language level, of which MLU is a canonical index.

**S-133** [local_879ec69b] — *Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning*

Whole-body movement kinematics, and the construct argument is one of the better ones in this review. Gait and gesture are presented as 'prominent behavioural markers' that can be 'efficiently and non-intrusively captured', and the case for preferring them to language-based assessment is made explicitly: diagnosis 'often requires speech-based tests', yet at the early detection stage 'many young children may not yet be able to speak'. That identifies a genuine coverage gap - the transcript-based and conversational measures charted elsewhere in this review are inapplicable to non-speaking and pre-verbal children, who are precisely the population early detection targets. The operationalisation is only partly matched to the argument. In the Gait dataset the construct is walking, measured across 25 full-body joints, which is the right instrument for the claim. In DREAM only 10 upper-body joints are available and the movements arise from therapy interaction, so gait is not measurable and the second experiment addresses a different construct under the same label. And no interpretability analysis connects the models to any nameable movement characteristic, so what aspect of gait the 95.4% reflects - stride variability, arm swing, postural sway, turning - is unknown, despite skeleton data making such an analysis unusually accessible.

**S-134** [local_93e5d23d] — *Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]*

Cry acoustics, and specifically voice quality rather than cry structure. Three perturbation measures were analysed - jitter, shimmer and harmonics-to-noise ratio - selected because of their established clinical use in voice assessment. The construct choice is the study's strongest conceptual contribution and is unique in this review: cry is available before any language develops, is produced by every child regardless of cognitive or verbal level, requires no cooperation, no task compliance and no social engagement, and directly reflects neuromuscular control of the larynx and respiratory system. The paper's formulation is apt - 'infant cries provide a unique window into the neurological and physiological state of the infant' - and it identifies prior work reporting atypical cry acoustics in autistic toddlers under 18 months, which is younger than any other behavioural measure charted here can reach. The findings are physiologically legible: higher jitter and shimmer mean greater cycle-to-cycle instability in the frequency and amplitude of vocal fold vibration, and lower harmonics-to-noise ratio means a greater proportion of aperiodic energy, so the composite picture is of less stable phonatory control. Two constructs are conspicuously not addressed: the temporal and prosodic structure of the cry, which prior work also implicates, and the communicative function of crying, which is discarded when only 'pure crying sounds' are retained.

**S-135** [local_a0d73248] — *Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm*

None observed. The A1-A10 fields are a respondent's answers to ten statements about their own social-communication characteristics, and the remaining fields are registration metadata. These are self-characterisations rather than records of behaviour produced, which is the distinction this review applies when admitting app telemetry, written language or nurse-recorded milestone attainment as behavioural data.

**S-136** [local_4ceee075] — *Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics*

The broadest simultaneous behavioural coverage from a single camera in this review: facial configuration and expression through a 468-point face mesh, whole-body posture through 33 pose points, and manual gesture through 21 points per hand, all captured at 30 frames per second and reduced to a 1,639-value vector per frame. Two derived measures add interpretable structure. The mouth aspect ratio - the ratio of vertical to horizontal lip distance - is a compact index of mouth opening that relates to both expression and vocalisation. Motion energy, defined as the mean Euclidean displacement of landmark coordinates between consecutive frames and computed separately for the face, the pose and each hand, is a clean measure of how much each body region moves per unit time, and its per-region computation means motor activity can be localised rather than aggregated. The stated behavioural targets - reduced eye contact, atypical emotional expression, and repetitive stereotypical movement - map reasonably onto these streams, though gaze itself is not measured directly and stereotypy is not identified as such, only as elevated hand motion energy. The visualisations reported (heat maps and movement-energy graphs) show group differences in motor activity and facial expression, but no ablation determines which stream the classifier uses, which leaves the construct claim unresolved.

**S-137** [local_84bcd4ed] — *Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of*

Two constructs of very different tractability. For autism, static facial appearance and expression, with the usual consequence that the model receives everything an uncontrolled photograph contains - morphology, expression at the captured instant, pose, apparent age, ancestry, resolution and image provenance - and no analysis identifies which of these it uses. For gelotophobia, the paper proposes to read a dispositional social fear from a still facial image. This is the weakest construct mapping in the review and its weakness is structural rather than a matter of execution: gelotophobia is defined by how a person interprets laughter directed at them, it is measured by self-report for that reason, and no laughter, social interaction or ridicule appears anywhere in the data. The paper's own finding that DeepFace 'was insufficient' for ambiguous facial cues, and its observation that fear and disgust involve minimal facial muscle movement, both point toward the same conclusion without stating it - that the construct is not visible in a photograph. The fallback offered is the GELOPH<15> self-report, which is the appropriate instrument and which the study did not administer.

**S-138** [local_d97673f4] — *Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection*

Nominally craniofacial morphology and operationally whatever separates two internet image folders. The motivating claims are unusually specific - wider eyes, larger mouth, shorter mid-face, broader upper face, pronounced philtrum, shorter nose - and none is measured: no landmarks are detected, no distances or ratios computed, and the models receive whole preprocessed face crops. The three preprocessing configurations do bear on this indirectly and constitute the study's most interesting technical choice: greyscale conversion removes colour and therefore skin tone, and CLAHE normalises local contrast, so the greyscale-plus-CLAHE configuration strips two of the appearance cues most likely to differ between image sources. Comparing configurations that differ in exactly which appearance information is retained is the right instinct for this problem, and a systematic report of accuracy across the three would have been informative about how much of the signal survives when colour and illumination are removed. That comparison is set up and its results are not broken out in the retrieved text.

**S-139** [local_86a67a4f] — *Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children*

Two constructs, of very different tractability. The autism task targets facial morphology, on the premise that autistic children 'show morphological differences within their face' - a physiognomic claim, unmeasured here, with the models receiving whole face images so that expression, pose, apparent age, ancestry and image provenance are all equally available. The emotion task targets six-way facial expression in autistic children specifically, and the construct argument for it is the paper's strongest contribution: general-population emotion models are 'primarily trained for healthy ones and consequently missing abnormal facial movements'. That correctly identifies a real gap, and the resulting 73.33% is instructive precisely because it is modest - emotion recognition on posed neurotypical adult faces reaches 98-99% in the benchmark literature charted elsewhere in this review, so a drop to the low seventies on autistic children's faces is consistent with the independent finding that affect models transfer poorly across this population. Read together with that study, this one supplies a second data point for the same conclusion.

**S-140** [local_0a39cca9] — *Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy*

Facial appearance, described more honestly than in most of this branch. Rather than asserting a specific craniofacial phenotype, the paper says the network finds 'important patterns in the image, such as the shape of the face, the expression on it, and the texture of the skin'. That enumeration is accurate about what a whole-image CNN actually receives, and it names two properties - expression and skin texture - that are not morphological and would vary with photographic circumstance rather than with the child. Naming skin texture as a used feature is particularly pointed in a corpus mixing an internationally scraped collection with photographs from an Indonesian clinic, since skin appearance in an image is jointly determined by ancestry, lighting and camera. No landmark geometry or morphometric quantity is computed anywhere.

**S-141** [local_7432ffd7] — *Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models*

Visual attention allocation during free viewing - fixation position (point of regard, left and right eye), gaze direction vectors in three dimensions, and the categorical annotation of what was being looked at (Category_Right, Category_Left) alongside stimulus identity. The behavioural construct is therefore where the child looks, sampled instantaneously, with no aggregation into fixations, saccades, dwell times or AOI proportions.

**S-142** [local_8ff20c48] — *Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning*

Early social-communication behaviours as reported by a caregiver: response to name, ease of eye contact, requesting gestures, declarative pointing, pretend play, gaze following, comforting a distressed family member, early speech quality, conventional gestures such as waving goodbye, and prolonged purposeless staring. After correlation-based deletion only five of these (A3 requesting gestures, A4 pointing, A5 pretend play, A7 comforting, A10 staring) remain as predictors.

**S-143** [local_986436f2] — *Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost*

Static facial morphology rather than behaviour: inter-landmark geometry and facial asymmetry, operationalised as upper-face breadth, eye spacing, mid-face length and jawline shape, over landmarks at the eye corners, eyebrows, nose tip, mouth corners and jaw outline. The theoretical warrant offered is that discrepancies in facial landmarks between those with ASD and those without indicate underlying variances in brain development.

**S-144** [local_bb4d1f7a] — *Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models*

Visual attention during viewing of a speaking face, decomposed into fixation position (x, y), fixation duration and inter-fixation velocity, and into scanpath shape compared by DTW and MultiMatch. The behavioural claims that emerge are specific and testable: attention duration and vertical gaze distribution differ most across severity levels, velocity least, and children with ASD show highly individualised rather than merely reduced gaze patterns.

**S-145** [local_13c1f46d] — *Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism*

None. No behaviour is observed, elicited or measured. The target is static facial appearance - edges, contours and textures at multiple Gabor orientations and scales, described as capturing intricate details of face characteristics including the eyes, nose and mouth.

**S-146** [local_e771fb69] — *Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data*

Movement kinematics and eye-movement behaviour, split into general and attention-specific variants: 120 kinematic features and 48 observational-behavioural features per instructional segment, with the attention-specific eye subset described as covering fixation and saccade characteristics. Because no task is described and no feature is ever named, the behavioural content of the study is opaque - the reader cannot identify a single behaviour that distinguishes the groups.

**S-147** [local_945300a5] — *Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network*

Posed facial expression - flat, smiling and sad - and, implicitly, static facial appearance. Because expressions are pooled before classification, the study cannot say whether the model distinguishes groups by how the children produce expressions or by how their faces look, and the paper does not raise the distinction.

**S-148** [local_ed30e24c] — *Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI*

Parent-reported early social-communication behaviours drawn from Q-CHAT-10. The SHAP analysis names three specifically: joint attention (does your child follow where you are looking), use of simple gestures, and empathy-related behaviours. These are clinically sensible early markers, and the paper notes correctly that they correspond to established clinical markers - but their prominence in the model is a property of how the label was constructed, not independent evidence about them.

**S-149** [local_b9de0d7f] — *Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques*

Parent-reported early social-communication behaviours from Q-CHAT-10 - response to name, eye contact, gestures, pointing, pretend play, gaze following, comforting, early speech, staring. No behaviour is observed, and the physical and verbal performance invoked in the Phase II framing does not exist in the data.

**S-150** [local_14df790d] — *Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach*

Parent-reported early social-communication behaviours from the Q-CHAT: response to name, ease of eye contact, pointing to express desires, and the remaining seven items, each mapped to a DSM-5 behavioural domain. The item-level analysis produces a consistent ordering - Q9, Q6 and Q5 most informative, Q8 and Q10 least - which is the paper's substantive behavioural claim.

**S-151** [local_4da2b941] — *Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study*

Camouflaging behaviour, decomposed into compensation (copying others' behaviours, preparing scripts for social situations), masking (controlling and adjusting facial and bodily expression to fit in) and assimilation (effortful engagement and pretending to be normal in social situations). The outcomes are dimensional autistic traits - aloof personality, pragmatic language, rigid personality - and depressive and anxious symptoms. The behaviour of interest is therefore an active social strategy rather than a deficit, and the study is the only one in the corpus to treat an autistic behaviour as adaptive rather than symptomatic.

**S-152** [local_6e7174c0] — *A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach*

None. The classification target is static facial appearance. The paper's own account of what the model attends to - periocular regions, eye gaze, mouth movements, asymmetric facial movements - describes dynamic behaviours that a single photograph cannot contain, so the stated biomarker rationale and the actual input are mismatched.

**S-153** [local_e04bcd32] — *Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network*

None. No behaviour is observed, elicited or measured. The target is static facial appearance recovered from deblurring and denoising.

**S-154** [local_183eaef4] — *Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI*

Autistic traits as captured by the ten AQ-10 items, characterised in the XAI discussion as communication patterns, repetitive actions and frequency of eye contact. All behaviour is second-hand and questionnaire-mediated, reported by a family member, healthcare professional or unspecified other.

**S-155** [local_b6ac2b98] — *Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks*

Social attention during simultaneous presentation of social and non-social stimuli: preferential looking to faces versus objects, indexed by fixation duration, fixation count, visit duration and latency to first fixation, across areas of interest from whole-stimulus categories down to eyes and mouth and across three emotional expressions. The substantive behavioural finding is about objects rather than faces - mean duration of visits to objects discriminates, which the authors interpret as difficulty disengaging attention from objects rather than as reduced interest in faces.

**S-156** [local_44d3aef5] — *Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis*

Visual scanning behaviour, encoded as a rendered scanpath image showing the geometric trace of fixations and saccades. Because the images are treated as pictures rather than as sequences, no fixation duration, saccade amplitude, area-of-interest dwell or temporal ordering is extracted or reported - the behavioural content of the data is entirely implicit in the picture.

**S-157** [local_24fefc5f] — *A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection*

Parent-reported early social-communication behaviour, entirely unspecified - the article names the Q-CHAT-10 instrument and describes its scoring rule but never states or discusses a single item, so no behaviour is identified anywhere in the paper.

**S-158** [local_69b10fe4] — *An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms*

Fine motor kinematics during constrained tracing: speed, acceleration, jerk, minimum and maximum speed, number of sub-movements, speed modulation (how sharply speed adapts to trajectory curvature), smoothness via SPARC, and tracing error, plus simple reaction time. The discriminating features are specific and directional - autistic participants showed greater speed modulation and more sub-movements than both other groups, and differed from PD in reaction time - and the paper is careful about mechanism, noting that reported increases in jerk in autism may be epiphenomenal on speed differences because the two quantities are mathematically linked.

**S-159** [local_af9f4c12] — *An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data*

Screening-item behaviours from the A1-A10 instruments, organised into three domains - social communication difficulties, repetitive behaviour and a cognitive assessment component - which supply the weighted terms of the constructed severity index. The correlation analysis relates the composite Q_SCORE to social communication difficulties (r 0.64-0.67) and repetitive behaviour (r 0.45-0.63) and reports moderate inter-item correlations (r 0.10-0.46), read as each item adding unique variance.

**S-160** [local_367db0b6] — *An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns*

Developmental screening behaviours as captured by ASQ, CSBS, PEDS, M-CHAT and STAT items - communication through eye movements and repetitive hand and finger movements are the only behaviours described concretely - together with imaging and physiological modalities named but not characterised.

**S-161** [local_8d43288c] — *Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos*

Self-stimulatory motor behaviour observed in natural settings: arm flapping, head banging and spinning, against a fourth class of non-stereotyped movement. This is the corpus's clearest instance of behaviour being observed directly rather than inferred from a photograph, a checklist or a questionnaire - the behaviours are the ones clinicians actually watch for, recorded where they actually occur. The confusion-matrix analysis adds a substantive behavioural observation: errors concentrate between spinning and the two repetitive classes, attributed to overlap in motion dynamics, and normal behaviour is moderately confused with the repetitive classes in the held-out test.

**S-162** [local_5f57ba19] — *Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension*

Social attention to a speaking face, decomposed by facial region and by time relative to speech onset: fixation count, average fixation duration, dwell-time and fixation-time percentages, normalised dwell coverage and revisits, for the eyes, mouth and nose separately. The substantive behavioural findings are specific and testable - eye revisits and mouth fixation count rank highest in importance, mouth fixation time and cross-AOI revisits emerge as candidate biomarkers under both attribution methods, and the audio-visual advantage is concentrated in the pre-speech phase, which the authors read as anticipatory attention to the mouth before speech begins.

**S-163** [local_1d856900] — *Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare*

Dataset 1: screening-questionnaire responses and comorbidity flags, none of them examined individually. Dataset 2: the most behaviourally specific description in the paper - velocity, acceleration, jerk, movement range, coordination and repetitive behavioural patterns from body keypoints, alongside voice quality and autonomic arousal - describing exactly the kind of multimodal behavioural measurement this literature needs, for a dataset whose existence the paper does not evidence.

**S-164** [local_7b19a959] — *Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis*

Neuropsychological performance across three domains rather than a single behavioural marker: multisensory perceptual integration, emotion recognition (with accuracy and reaction time varying by emotional category and stimulus type), and executive function. The substantive behavioural findings are specific - reaction-time variables consistently ranked high in predictive value, and executive function emerged as informative in this adult sample - and the paper is careful that the ranking is sample-dependent.

**S-165** [local_d7b6fa00] — *Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath*

Visual scanning behaviour reduced to nine interpretable descriptors: number of fixations, mean and maximum and first fixation duration, total fixation duration, total path length, mean saccade amplitude, spatial dispersion of fixations, and fixation-duration entropy as a measure of irregularity in gaze allocation. Operating on these rather than on rendered scanpath images is the paper's central methodological claim, and it is a defensible one - the features are inspectable and the permutation analysis can name which of them matter.

**S-166** [local_e54c304c] — *Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models*

None. No behaviour is observed or measured; the target is static facial appearance, described in terms of symmetry, eye spacing, philtrum width and face shape.

**S-167** [local_e4c2a776] — *Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images*

None. No behaviour is observed or measured. The targets are static facial features enhanced by Gabor filtering, with the paper referring to facial cues relevant to ASD and to expression patterns and facial morphology without identifying any specific feature.

**S-168** [local_231757c7] — *SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers*

Motor function measured directly in three dimensions: inter-joint distances, range of motion, gait speed, step length and cycle time, and temporal characteristics, over 25 skeletal joints. The behavioural claims arising from SHAP are anatomically specific - wrist movements, knee trajectories and elbow-to-foot distances - and are related to motor impairments reported in the prior ASD literature rather than presented as novel discoveries. A structural pattern is also reported: Y-axis features decline (30% to 10% to 0%) and X-axis features increase (70% to 90% to 100%) with increasing severity, though the severe end of that gradient is synthetic.

**S-169** [local_1b457442] — *Screening autism spectrum*

Expressive language and conversational participation in spontaneous interaction. The two leading features are behaviourally specific and directionally interpretable: Mean Length of Utterance, where lower values indicate shorter and simpler utterances and are associated with higher ASD likelihood, and Mean Length of Turn Ratio, the child's turn length relative to the adult's, where lower values indicate that the child contributes less to conversational exchange. Both correspond to well-established clinical observations, and the paper relates them accordingly rather than presenting them as discoveries.

**S-170** [local_b26db2f2] — *Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches*

Executive function as elicited by three purpose-built games - planning, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, working memory and performance monitoring - captured through session-level telemetry including duration and task-performance fields. This is behaviour observed during a designed task rather than reported on a checklist or inferred from an appearance, and the construct is theoretically motivated rather than chosen for convenience. What the paper does not do is say which behaviours distinguished the groups: no feature importance is reported, so the executive-function framing that justifies the whole design is never connected to a result.

---

## RQ3.2 — Multimodal fusion

_170 of 170 studies charted for this question._

**S-001** [local_76fc33d0] — *Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers*

Single modality; no fusion. No combination with clinical scores or demographics.

**S-002** [local_0dbc5018] — *Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities*

Single modality; no fusion across behavioral modalities. IQ and chronological age are used as ANCOVA covariates in the group comparison but are not combined with kinematics in the classifier.

**S-003** [local_dc5fc4bb] — *ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data*

Two behavioral streams (correctness and latency) are combined by simple feature concatenation (RC&RT) and compared against each separately - an early-fusion feature-level combination. No integration with clinical scores, demographics or parent report.

**S-004** [local_863980f8] — *Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework*

Single modality; no fusion is performed. The discussion explicitly proposes future multimodal fusion with physiological, speech, motion and facial-expression measures. Within the modality, image-level decisions are fused to a participant-level decision by averaging confidence scores - a late/decision-level fusion across stimuli rather than across modalities.

**S-005** [local_be8aa62f] — *Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder*

Single modality. Positive and negative descriptions are analysed both combined and separately (the network difference loses significance when split, which the authors attribute to reduced power). Demographic and cognitive variables (age, gender, verbal IQ, vocabulary, WMS) are added to the classifier as covariates and do not improve performance - an integration attempt that is reported as null rather than omitted.

**S-006** [local_e404a2a3] — *Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism*

Two behavioral data streams from the same device - touch and inertial - are combined by feature concatenation into a single 247-dimensional vector (early/feature-level fusion). Predictions from the two games are additionally averaged per child, a decision-level fusion across tasks that produced the best AUC (0.932) - higher than either game alone. Age and gender are included as features in ET, RF and RGF, and deliberately excluded in RGF2, which performed best, showing the result does not depend on demographic inputs.

**S-007** [local_780141fc] — *Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study*

Single modality; no fusion across behavioral modalities. Within the modality there is a form of condition-level fusion: features from the two best conditions (No-Target Fast and No-Target Elevated) are combined into a joint 40-feature vector, which raised Naive Bayes accuracy from 70.0% and 66.7% individually to 83.3% jointly - an explicit demonstration that combining task conditions helps. IQ and age are used as matching variables, not as model inputs.

**S-008** [local_3a331973] — *Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data*

Six behavioral feature families are combined by concatenation into a single normalised vector before classification - early/feature-level fusion - with temporal structure preserved by computing each family separately per story segment and concatenating across the 12 segments, which the authors describe as trading a twelvefold dimensionality increase for retained temporal information. No integration with clinical scores or demographics.

**S-009** [local_7b3e6b3a] — *Earlier identification of children with autism*

Single modality; no fusion. Video was recorded but used only for segmentation and annotation, not as a modelling input - a notable choice given that the same recordings could have supported gaze or motor analysis. Within the modality, per-vocalisation decisions are aggregated into a subject-level judgement by computing an ASD ratio and thresholding it, which is a late/decision-level fusion across utterances.

**S-010** [local_36aa3ace] — *Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative*

Single modality; no fusion. Two acoustic feature sets are compared rather than combined, and no combination with clinical, cognitive or demographic data is performed. The future-work section proposes extending the approach to video and physiological signals, but no multimodal work is done here.

**S-011** [local_44b58f21] — *ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces*

Single modality, but with a form of within-modality fusion: features from all three orthogonal GRF components (medial-lateral, anterior-posterior, vertical) are pooled into one candidate set, and the three surviving features happen to come one from each component - so the discriminative signal is genuinely distributed across all three force directions. No combination with clinical, cognitive or demographic data.

**S-012** [local_cb9a5b48] — *Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening*

Two feature families derived from the same modality - similarity of time-weighted spatial occupancy patterns, and the presence ratio in the robot-facing cell - are each fed to separate first-layer classifiers whose outputs are combined by a second-layer classifier. The authors describe this explicitly as a form of sensor fusion, though both inputs come from one sensor; it is decision-level fusion across feature views. Notably the fusion helped only the SVM (75% and 75% to 81.3%) and hurt the other four classifiers (dropping to 68.8%). No integration with clinical scores, demographics or parent report.

**S-013** [local_40cd7d53] — *Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children*

Single modality; no fusion. Within the modality, ten regional fixation times plus three derived ratios are supplied jointly to the SVM, which is feature-level combination across regions. Gaze data are separately correlated with Gesell developmental subscores using age and gender as covariates - an integration with clinical measures for interpretation rather than for prediction.

**S-014** [local_5b1d0b36] — *Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday*

Fusion is the paper's central methodological claim and is done at two levels. Across modalities: acoustic and linguistic features are extracted separately and concatenated. Across sources: features from four structured tests plus passive monitoring plus usage pattern are all concatenated into one 1330-dimensional vector, with missing sources explicitly encoded as -1 so the model can handle non-participation rather than requiring imputation. The benefit is quantified by ablation - every single source scored 0.47-0.77 alone against 0.87 fused - and confirmed by CFS selecting at least one feature from each source, which the authors correctly note implies the sources are complementary rather than redundant given CFS's redundancy penalty. No integration with clinical scores or demographics, deliberately.

**S-015** [local_54954c19] — *Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching*

Single modality. Gaze features are combined at feature level with non-gaze contextual variables (page identity, AOI identity, correct-answer location, gender, visual complexity), and the paper reports that these additions generally reduced accuracy relative to gaze features alone - a negative fusion result reported plainly. Behaviour-level predictions are aggregated to a participant-level decision by majority vote, a late fusion across observations. The discussion proposes future fusion with non-gaze interaction data (mouse clicks, operation logs) as a route to eye-tracker-free deployment.

**S-016** [local_d8dc996a] — *Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection*

Single modality, no fusion. There is a form of temporal-spatial integration internal to the model - the LSTM's learned attention map weights spatial CNN features at each time step based on its accumulated hidden state, so spatial and temporal information are combined adaptively rather than by fixed pooling. Frame-level probabilities are averaged into a per-subject decision, a late fusion across frames and clips. No combination with clinical scores, IQ or demographics, despite those being available.

**S-017** [local_88ddfdd1] — *A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task*

Single modality, but with an unusual internal contrast: spatial-only and spatial-plus-temporal representations of the same data are constructed through identical pipelines and compared, which is a form of ablation rather than fusion. Left and right eye representations are kept separate and both included as features, motivated by a possible lateral offset with each eye directed slightly toward its own side of the face. Face emotion, gender, age and task type were tested as additional predictors and reported as not significantly improving either model.

**S-018** [local_361110f1] — *Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features*

Single modality; no fusion. Within the modality, three kinematic quantities (amplitude, velocity, acceleration) are each summarised by two complexity measures (entropy and 95% range) and three cross-trial aggregates (min, median, max), giving an 18-feature grid, and the selected model combines amplitude-range and velocity-range/entropy features - so the fusion is across kinematic derivatives and trial aggregates. The discussion proposes future integration with genetic, neuroimaging and psychological data.

**S-019** [local_51533de4] — *Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations*

Two-way fusion. Across modality: 352 acoustic and 272 text features are concatenated into a single 624-dimensional vector, then reduced by correlation filtering and PCA - so acoustic and lexical information are combined at feature level. Across speaker: features from the child and the confederate are both included, and the results show confederate features were selected in all 70 folds for several jitter and HNR measures, making interlocutor behaviour an explicit part of the model. Demographic and clinical variables were tested as additional inputs and reported as unhelpful (age and sex) or harmful (IQ), which the authors correctly attribute to prior matching - a negative fusion result reported rather than omitted.

**S-020** [local_96c87d36] — *Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking*

Feature-level fusion across the three families into a single per-fixation vector, and the contribution of each is ablated separately at fixation, trial and subject level - so the complementarity claim is directly evidenced. The clearest demonstration is that task features alone reach 81.0% subject-level accuracy but only 56.5% sensitivity, while adding gaze and face features raises sensitivity to 91.3% at similar accuracy. Predictions are additionally fused across observations by soft voting from fixations to trials to subjects, with accuracy rising monotonically (72.5% to 75.6% to 86.2%) as the aggregation unit widens.

**S-021** [local_4b031d44] — *Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine*

Fusion occurs across annotators rather than across modalities, and this is the paper's methodological contribution. Each rater's annotations train a separate random forest, and predictions are combined by a softmax-weighted ensemble whose weights reflect each rater's model accuracy relative to a majority-vote baseline. The authors argue this lets the ensemble exploit each rater's strengths (one may rate eye contact well, another language ability) while discounting their weaknesses, and note it permits distributed annotation where each rater sees only a subset of videos without requiring imputation. A second form of composition is the stacked two-layer architecture, where layer one's atypical classifications feed layer two.

**S-022** [local_05ef29e5] — *Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification*

Single behavioural modality, but with genuine cross-source integration: three feature families (image content, fixation behaviour, centre bias) are concatenated for the classifier, and two of them require fusing gaze data with image-analysis outputs (YOLO object masks and SDSP saliency maps). This gaze-plus-stimulus-content fusion is a distinctive design in the corpus, though its contribution is never ablated so the value of each family is unknown. No integration with clinical, cognitive or demographic data - the latter being impossible given the dataset.

**S-023** [local_9528024b] — *Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol*

Multiple cue types are combined within each task's observation set and jointly update a shared belief over child condition, engagement and verbal activity - so eye contact, utterances, imitation and gestures fuse probabilistically into one latent state estimate. The hierarchical structure adds a second fusion level: each task's terminal belief is discretised into a partition index that becomes an observation for the protocol-level model, so information accumulates across tasks. This belief-space-partitioning interface is the paper's central technical contribution and is a genuinely different fusion mechanism from the feature concatenation used everywhere else in the corpus.

**S-024** [local_6230fe22] — *Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism*

Single modality, no fusion. Per-ROI mean fixation durations are concatenated into a single feature vector per participant, described as capturing the time distribution of visual attention across regions - a within-modality spatial aggregation rather than multimodal fusion. No integration with clinical scores, demographics or the medical-history data the workflow collects.

**S-025** [local_785ba418] — *Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis*

Single modality, but with two distinct feature families combined - movement kinematics and endpoint accuracy - which is what allows the speed-accuracy trade-off to emerge. Features from dominant and non-dominant hands are pooled into means and standard deviations, a form of within-modality aggregation. No integration with clinical, cognitive or demographic data.

**S-026** [local_fea042be] — *Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual*

Single modality, but with an internal fusion of four kinematic quantities into one image: spatial path as line geometry, velocity as the red channel, acceleration as green and jerk as blue. This packs position and its first three temporal derivatives into a single representation that a generic image classifier can consume - an elegant encoding, though the subsequent grayscale conversion collapses the three colour channels back into a single luminance value, discarding the channel separation the encoding created.

**S-027** [local_ba5fbda7] — *Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD*

Single modality in this analysis. The parent study measured interpersonal coordination between dyad members, but this classification uses intrapersonal synchrony only. Features from four separate interaction tasks are aggregated per participant, a form of fusion across contexts. The future-work section explicitly proposes multimodal fusion with eye-gaze, facial expression and clinical questionnaire data, and Box 1 lists 'combination of objective variables and standard diagnostic measures as input features' as a minimum requirement for reliable clinical application.

**S-028** [local_7b468950] — *Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart*

Two synchronous sensor streams from a single consumer device - touch-screen contact patterns and triaxial accelerometer plus gyroscope - capturing both what the child does to the screen and how the device moves while they do it. The fusion is inherent to the platform rather than engineered, which is part of the design's practical appeal: no synchronisation, no calibration and no additional hardware is required to obtain two complementary views of the same motor behaviour.

**S-029** [local_309e5baa] — *Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns*

Two forms of fusion. In the synthetic saccade approach, real and synthetic scanpaths are aligned by dynamic time warping and concatenated along with aggregate duration statistics and three trajectory distance measures - fusing observed behaviour with a model-generated reference. In the image-based approach, a two-branch architecture separately encodes the stimulus image (frozen pretrained ResNet-18) and the fixation channels (ResNet-18 with a 33-channel input layer), concatenating their 512-dimensional outputs into a 1024-dimensional vector - fusing stimulus content with gaze behaviour. Both are stimulus-plus-behaviour fusions rather than multi-behavioural fusions.

**S-030** [local_a45f39e9] — *Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time*

Single modality in this work. Within it, the PoTion representation performs a spatiotemporal fusion: keypoint heatmaps from up to 301 frames are colourised by body region and by relative time, then aggregated into one image, so a 10-second motion sequence is compressed into a single static RGB frame that a standard convolutional classifier can consume. The colour channels carry body-region identity and the intensity gradient carries temporal order, which is an elegant encoding of three information types into three channels. Future fusion with RGB appearance and audio is proposed.

**S-031** [local_d587f9cd] — *Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning*

Spatial rather than modal fusion, and it is the architecture's central idea. Multiple RGBD cameras each estimate head pose and gaze independently and publish them as ROS odometry messages; a fusion node performs asynchronous matching across all local estimates and computes a single visual focus of attention through a Hidden Markov Model, published with a timestamp and the name of the attention target. Fusing viewpoints to recover a gaze target is a direct answer to the occlusion problem that limits single-camera gaze measurement with moving children - the paper reports occlusion 'by hair, hands and the robot' as encountered in practice - and the HMM adds temporal smoothing so that the attention target is inferred from a sequence rather than frame by frame. No other study in this review builds comparable measurement infrastructure, and the fact that it is assembled from open-source components on ROS makes it reproducible in principle.

**S-032** [local_08b8027d] — *SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths*

Fusion of behavioural and stimulus-derived information at two levels. Per fixation, a 1024-dimensional CNN encoding of the saliency-map patch is concatenated with the fixation duration, giving a 1025-dimensional vector that combines spatial-saliency context with temporal information. Across fixations, a two-layer LSTM integrates the sequence, explicitly to capture 'the temporal information and sequential dependency of the scanpaths'. No fusion across behavioural modalities and no integration with clinical or demographic data - the latter being impossible given the dataset.

**S-033** [local_c6f1209b] — *Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children*

None. A single video stream coded by human raters, with the robot's own sensors unused for measurement. The paper's engineering framing points toward using them - it is explicitly gathering requirements for an 'interaction diagnosis system' - but no automated sensing is implemented here.

**S-034** [local_83b99e73] — *Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers*

No multimodal fusion. All features come from a single modality (video-coded social behaviour). The study's structural comparison is instead across conditions of the same modality: the still-face episode versus the free-interaction episode, and the still-face episode won for every classifier (83.35 vs 81.18 for SVM, 83.13 vs 80.72 for random forest, 82.35 vs 80.54 for naive Bayes). This is a useful counterpoint to the corpus's fusion studies - here the gain comes from choosing a better elicitation condition rather than adding a sensor.

**S-035** [local_638860ef] — *Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis*

Explicit multimodal fusion with quantified benefit: kinematic features alone gave 73%, eye movement features alone 70%, and combined features 78%. The authors state that the modalities 'provided complementary information for predictions', and the 5-point gain over the better single modality is one of the clearest quantified fusion benefits in the corpus, obtained under independent testing rather than internal cross-validation. Features are combined at feature level before selection and classification.

**S-036** [local_7547db68] — *Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network*

No multimodal fusion. Adding recognition of children's physical movement to achieve 'diagnosis of autism from multiple perspectives' is named as future work. There is a nominal model-level combination - VGG-19 and ResNet-18 are said to be trained and then 'synthesised' - but no mechanism, weighting or comparative result is given for either model separately, so the combination cannot be evaluated.

**S-037** [local_878c259f] — *Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach*

Single modality, but with a designed within-modality manipulation: the same six COP variables are measured under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions and both sets are supplied jointly to the classifiers, giving 12 features. This effectively fuses two sensory conditions, allowing the models to exploit how each child's sway changes when visual input is removed. No integration with clinical, cognitive or demographic data, though anthropometrics were collected.

**S-038** [local_1579c85a] — *Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through*

Feature-level fusion of the two modalities: 3 Laban movement features are concatenated with 68 facial keypoints into a single 71-dimensional vector per 1-second window, so movement and facial information are combined before classification. There is no ablation isolating either modality's contribution, so their relative value is unknown. The discussion proposes future fusion with physiological, eye gaze and vocal data.

**S-039** [local_157d6266] — *Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism*

Single modality, with a designed internal fusion: spatial distance and two temporal asynchrony measures (lag and advance) are combined by learned linear weights into one continuous score, so spatial and temporal aspects of imitation are integrated rather than treated separately. The authors argue this integration is necessary 'given the importance of timing in social coordination and in characterizing autism-specific imitation impairments'. Separately, the CAMI score is validated against and correlated with independent clinical instruments (ADOS-2, SRS-2, MABC-2), which is convergent validation rather than fusion.

**S-040** [local_8be557e3] — *Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation*

No multimodal fusion - audio only, and the paper notes that video recordings existed but only their audio was used. The structural comparison it does make is across feature representations of the same modality: raw eGeMAPS-88, statistically selected eGeMAPS-54, and learned auto-encoder bottleneck features. Extension to linguistic features alongside acoustic ones for older children is named as future work.

**S-041** [local_c79e100a] — *Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models*

No multimodal fusion. A single modality throughout. The paper's structural comparison is instead between two aggregation levels of the same modality - the gait cycle and the walking trial - which is a distinct axis from the sensor-fusion comparisons elsewhere in the corpus and arguably a more fundamental one, since it concerns what a data point is rather than what it contains.

**S-042** [local_4fecbf6d] — *Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network*

No cross-sensor fusion - audio only. But there is a meaningful within-modality fusion result with a clear cost: the conversational features cannot be computed on short sub-groups of segments because they require the entire recording, so FC-DNN models 2 and 3 and the CNN use only the 48 acoustic and prosodic features. The best models therefore discard exactly the feature family that correlates most strongly with social affect symptoms, and still outperform the 60-feature vector model - which suggests the gain from many sub-samples outweighs the loss of conversational information, and implies an architecture that could use both would do better still.

**S-043** [local_95abe653] — *Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning*

No multimodal fusion. Gaze only, with non-gaze metadata (AOI identity, media identity, correct-answer indicator, page visual complexity, participant gender) tested as additional variables and found in almost every case to reduce accuracy. That systematic negative result is itself the paper's fusion finding: on this data, adding non-gaze information hurt.

**S-044** [local_40168c96] — *Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based*

No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. There is within-modality feature fusion between learned CNN representations and handcrafted multi-level saliency features, and the ablation quantifies each family's contribution: removing CNN features costs 8.6 accuracy points, high-level semantic features 5.7, low-level 4.0 and mid-level 2.3. The paper closes by expressing the hope that the work 'can contribute to the development of multimodal approaches in the early detection and diagnosis of ASD', positioning gaze as one future component rather than a complete solution.

**S-045** [local_d3852378] — *Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder*

Multimodality here is in the stimulus rather than the sensing: a single depth camera captures movement, while visual, auditory and olfactory channels are added cumulatively to the environment. The results are informative and partly counterintuitive. For whole-body movement, discrimination is best under visual stimulation alone (89.36%) and degrades as modalities accumulate (74.47%, then 70.21%). For the head alone the pattern reverses, improving from 80.85% to 82.98% to 89.36% as sensory load rises. And pooling everything - all joints across all conditions - gives the worst result of any model at 70.21% with 45.45% sensitivity. The lesson transferable to the corpus's sensor-fusion studies is that indiscriminate aggregation across conditions and channels can destroy a localised signal.

**S-046** [local_df438dd2] — *Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening*

Genuinely multimodal, but with the modalities serving different functions rather than being fused as parallel evidence: audio drives temporal segmentation (locating each stimulus onset from its scripted keyword) while video drives measurement (detecting the face and classifying the expression). This division is the framework's structural idea - speech tells the system when to look, vision tells it what it sees - and it is what allows an unsegmented clinical recording to be parsed automatically. Within the vision branch there is a second fusion, between a 3D-CNN capturing temporal dynamics and a 2D-CNN capturing spatial detail, concatenated to 1024 dimensions before classification. No accuracy comparison between the branches is reported, so the contribution of each is unquantified.

**S-047** [local_cd9e45eb] — *Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism*

No cross-modal fusion; the study is gaze-only. What it does instead is the inverse of fusion and arguably more useful: it asks how much of a large multi-paradigm battery can be discarded. The result is that 89.9% of stimuli can be removed with modest accuracy loss, and the paradigm-level analysis shows the retained signal concentrates in Dyadic Bids and Theory of Mind, both of which include visual response latency features, while Biomotion also has latency features but lacks discrete ROI measures on heads, faces, eyes and bodies. The authors hypothesise that Dyadic Bids and Theory of Mind features subsume information available in the other paradigms - a redundancy argument that is the mirror image of the fusion arguments elsewhere in this corpus.

**S-048** [local_56237213] — *The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data*

The clearest and most cleanly reported fusion result in the corpus, precisely because both single-modality baselines are given: EEG alone 68%, gaze alone 75.89%, fused 85.44% with AUC rising from 0.865 to 0.93. That is close to a 10-point gain over the better single modality, and the authors' rationale for expecting it is specific rather than generic - EEG abnormalities are inconsistent across the autism spectrum, particularly in high-functioning presentations, whereas 'atypical face processing' has been found 'for all types of ASD', so the modalities should fail on different subgroups. There is a second, within-modality fusion as well: own-race faces alone gave 72.33% and other-race faces 66.67%, but combining both face types gave 75.89%, better than either. The caveat is that with no validation scheme and feature selection over a much larger EEG feature pool, the size of the fusion gain cannot be taken at face value, and the identity of the 32 selected features is not disclosed so complementarity cannot be verified.

**S-049** [local_f9a5195f] — *Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses*

The fusion result is negative and instructive. Gaze features alone gave the best behavioural performance (83.9% on trial 1 and on all trials), emotion confusion matrices alone performed at or below chance in two of three trials (6.5% and 35.5%), and combining all feature blocks gave 71.0% - worse than gaze alone. Adding emotion features to gaze reduced accuracy in most cells of the ablation grid. This is a rare demonstration in the corpus that multimodal combination can degrade rather than improve performance when one modality carries little signal and the feature-to-participant ratio is extreme. The critical comparison, though, is not between modalities but against the metadata baseline: age and gender alone reached 71.0% with P = .04, the same accuracy as the full model with a marginally better P value, so no combination of behavioural features demonstrably beat two demographic variables.

**S-050** [local_16a77fb0] — *Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)*

A clean modality comparison with an informative asymmetry. Voice alone reached AUC 0.77, facial expression 0.74 with all 17 action units and 0.65 with the domain-selected subset, gaze 0.63, and all three combined 0.78 - so fusion added essentially nothing over voice alone, and the combined result is carried by the two strong modalities. The gaze failure is diagnosed rather than glossed: appearance-based estimation from a webcam is judged insufficiently precise for the subtle differences reported in the eye-tracking literature, and the authors explicitly recommend state-of-the-art eye trackers to test whether gaze carries information in this paradigm. The comparison between domain-selected facial features (0.65) and all available action units (0.74) is also instructive - constraining features for interpretability cost about 9 AUC points, a trade-off the authors accepted deliberately for 'transparent and explainable diagnostic decisions'.

**S-051** [local_9c4af7a3] — *Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades*

No multimodal fusion - a single modality throughout, and no within-modality condition comparison is exploited either. The gap and overlap blocks are described and their latency difference noted, but the paradigm's defining contrast is never used as a feature or analysed as a group-by-condition interaction, which is the main analytic opportunity the design offers and the paper leaves unused.

**S-052** [local_b70dae32] — *An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model*

Two behavioural channels are combined, but through a probabilistic model rather than a learned fusion: the posterior for each severity category is computed as the product of P(category | joint attention) and P(category | imitation). No single-channel baseline is reported, so the contribution of combining them cannot be assessed, and no ablation is performed. More problematically, the product form assumes the two observables are conditionally independent given severity - an assumption the study's own architecture violates, since the imitation module only activates once the child has sustained gaze on a robot for five seconds, making imitation performance conditional on joint attention performance by construction. There are also two sensing modalities (robot camera gaze and Kinect depth), but these map one-to-one onto the two behaviours rather than being fused.

**S-053** [local_51a0af74] — *Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data*

No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. The combination that does occur is across time and across regions: nine segment-specific classifiers are ensembled, and the finding is that the whole is greater than any part, with every individual segment classifier below 75% while the best three-segment combination reaches it. This is a temporal rather than sensory fusion result, and it carries a clear message for the corpus's video-based studies - that a joint attention response is a sequence and that classifying any single moment of it underperforms classifying the sequence. The authors' own reading is that segments 1, 3 and 8 'present three fundamental stages of JA' and that 'the complete action process is necessary', though this identification comes from an exhaustive search rather than an a priori hypothesis.

**S-054** [local_d8d3037b] — *Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study*

No cross-modal fusion. What is combined is models rather than modalities: seven classifiers ensembled by probability averaging and majority voting, with the stated rationale that 'the best model that matches the pattern of this group of data well does not mean that it can be generalized to fit another group of data', so combining reduces variance and improves generalisation. That reasoning is sound and is borne out empirically - the ensemble's recall held at 0.81 then 0.77 across the two experiments while individual models swung from 0.81 to 0.55 (gradient boosting) or 0.44 to 0.00 (logistic regression). This is the corpus's clearest demonstration that ensembling buys stability under population shift, even though the underlying task here is not what the paper claims.

**S-055** [local_991fe435] — *Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task*

No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. The condition-level analysis serves the analogous purpose and yields a clear result: three-class accuracy falls from 81.08% to 78.4% using gaze cues alone and to 77.0% using non-gaze cues alone, so both cue families carry non-redundant information and the full set is better than either. This supports the paper's substantive claim that visual-orienting deficits in autism 'are not only tied to social cues but appear to be domain-general'. The behavioural analysis reinforces it: all three groups found face cues harder than arrow and finger cues, but the high-functioning group showed a cue-type effect on target dwell time that the low-functioning group did not, whose 'poor performance did not depend on the amount of social information contained in the cue picture'.

**S-056** [local_8692a64f] — *Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis*

No cross-modal fusion, but a within-session combination of eye and head channels from a single device, which is closer to fusion than most gaze studies here attempt. No ablation isolates the contribution of the head channel, though the correlation analysis identifies head-eye features among the most label-correlated, alongside the area0 gaze features. The temporal decomposition into five stages is a second axis of combination - features are computed per stage and pooled - but no analysis compares stages, so which phase of the animation carries the signal is not established despite the stage structure being built into the design.

**S-057** [local_4d6fac7e] — *Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network*

The corpus's most architecturally ambitious fusion, and the ablation is properly constructed. Single-modality baselines using identical features and pipeline give 0.7368 for EEG and 0.7895 for gaze, against 0.9500 fused - a gain of over 15 points on the better single modality. Two comparators isolate the mechanism: a conventional pipeline concatenating features with mRMR selection and SVM reaches 0.8100, and a ResNet18 over concatenated features reaches only 0.7000 despite far greater capacity, which the authors read as showing that 'simply and rudely cascading EEG and eye-tracking recordings cannot make good use of multi-modality information'. The graph formulation itself is the contribution: features are nodes, thresholded covariances are edges, so convolution operates over discovered inter-feature structure rather than over a flat concatenation. The interpretive payoff is the cross-modal edge analysis, which identifies EEG synchronisation as related to exotic face, joint attention and gaze-following features, and entropy measures as related to face, joint attention and social interaction features - relationships that exist despite the two signals being recorded at different times. The caveat is that all of this rests on an accuracy figure whose validation unit is not stated and appears not to be the participant.

**S-058** [local_30c622f2] — *Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model*

No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. The combination that matters is across levels of image representation, and the design makes this an explicit test rather than an implicit one. The three feature levels map onto the two mechanisms the paper is interested in: pixel-level features index bottom-up attention driven by image statistics, semantic-level features index top-down attention driven by prior knowledge, and object-level features sit between. The finding that the two semantic features survive selection only in the non-severe group, while pixel-level features survive in both, is a direct within-modality dissociation supporting the hypothesis that severity impairs top-down more than bottom-up attentional guidance.

**S-059** [local_bfc088c7] — *Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation*

A clean and well-quantified fusion result, with both single-modality baselines reported: fixation features alone reach 84.62%, session length features alone reach 84.62%, and combined they reach 92.31% - roughly an 8-point gain. What makes it more informative than most fusion claims in the corpus is that the two feature families are conceptually distinct rather than two views of the same signal: one measures where the child looked, the other how long the interaction took. The best three-feature model draws on both, taking total session length plus two fixation features. The finding that session length alone reaches 79.49% is the most consequential single number in the paper, since it implies most of the discriminative information is available without an eye tracker at all.

**S-060** [local_25e34bbd] — *Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification*

The fusion result is clearly negative and is reported without spin, which makes it useful. Combining feature families reduced performance in nearly every condition: for autism detection MFCC plus RASTA-PLP fell to 80.7% from 100% for either alone, and HNR plus SNR fell to 53.2%; for Down syndrome detection MFCC plus RASTA-PLP fell to 78.3%. The single exception is HNR plus GNE reaching 100% for autism-versus-Down-syndrome discrimination. The authors state the conclusion plainly: 'the combined feature set provides less performance when compared to the individual features, for most of the cases'. Given the sample size this is more likely a dimensionality effect than a substantive finding, but it stands in useful contrast to the widespread assumption elsewhere in this corpus that combining features or modalities helps.

**S-061** [local_4917150c] — *Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning*

No cross-modal fusion. What is fused is spatial and temporal information within a single representation: the scanpath image simultaneously carries where gaze travelled and how fast, with velocity encoded as greyscale gradient along each line. This is a genuinely different answer to the multimodality problem from the feature-concatenation approaches elsewhere in the corpus - the two information types are combined at the representation level before any learning occurs, and the MIC analysis is offered as evidence that the velocity channel carries real signal, since velocity correlates with CARS at 0.79 and is exactly what the colour encodes.

**S-062** [local_241ec2c2] — *Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking*

No cross-modal fusion. The combination is across feature families within a single modality, and the genetic algorithm's per-group selection is what makes it interpretable: the two models retain overlapping but non-identical feature sets, with distance-to-centre and biological-movement indicators appearing only in the autistic model and colour appearing only in the typically developing model. The authors' explanation for the biological-movement asymmetry is subtle and worth recording - the feature covers the whole region containing biological movement, and since typically developing attention 'is specifically more focused on the regions with people and faces' which are already captured by dedicated features, the broader region adds nothing for that group. That is a redundancy argument rather than an absence-of-effect argument, and it distinguishes a feature being uninformative from being subsumed.

**S-063** [local_36617ec5] — *Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis*

No cross-modal fusion of sensor streams, but the stimulus is genuinely multisensory - visual, auditory and olfactory channels are synchronised, with odour presence and intensity under programmatic control. The analytic combination is across feature families, and the hypothesis-contrast approach makes it systematic: eight predefined families are modelled separately so their discriminative value can be compared. The resulting ordering is informative. Coarse social-versus-non-social contrasts perform best - people versus items at 84%, adults versus items at 83%, children versus items at 82% - while fine-grained within-social contrasts perform worst, with adults' faces versus bodies reaching only 66% and kappa 0.25. The authors draw the correct conclusion, that macro-area definitions capture the signal but cannot resolve face-internal patterns, and recommend adding eye and mouth areas.

**S-064** [local_d8e804d6] — *Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms*

No multimodal fusion; a single modality analysed across three axes. What the design does combine is two measurement approaches to the same behaviour - human coding of whether gestures occurred and automated kinematic measurement of how they were executed - and the divergence between them is the paper's most valuable result. Blind human coders found no group difference in gesture frequency; automated tracking found significant differences in every kinematic measure. The authors generalise this appropriately: the 'human perceptual system is good at detecting specific patterns of movement (e.g., head nodding, smiling), but it is not good at giving precise metric measures of movement', so pose tracking has 'an advantage over behavioral coding techniques - finding motor patterns that might be difficult to spot through human observations'. That is a specific, testable claim about what automation adds, and it is demonstrated within a single study.

**S-065** [local_712542ca] — *Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset*

No multimodal fusion. The only combination performed is unsupervised partitioning followed by supervised classification, which is a pipeline rather than a fusion. The result - higher accuracy within one cluster than on the pooled data - is presented as evidence that clustering helps, but no cluster is characterised, no analysis explains what makes cluster 1 different, and the improvement is a maximum over 36 cluster-by-classifier combinations, so it cannot be distinguished from selection across the grid.

**S-066** [local_0ab41681] — *Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder*

No multimodal fusion. What the study combines is levels of description within a single modality, and it does so to informative effect: the 17 classifier features include both conventional kinematics and the three synergy measures, and the per-participant feature importance analysis finds that spatial displacement measures and the cumulative variance accounted for by three components both contribute. The authors note that this 'substantially confirmed the results obtained with univariate statistics', so the classifier's internal weighting agrees with the group-level analysis - a convergence that few studies in the corpus check and that here supports treating the classification as reflecting the same phenomenon as the hypothesis test rather than an unrelated pattern.

**S-067** [local_9ca9b2cc] — *Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment*

Three streams combined into one running score - face detection, ear-based head orientation, and speech-response latency - fused by weighted accumulation with operator-set constants rather than by a learned combiner.
